policy: Nothing here is applied silently: tools/build_webkit_jsc.py verifies the SHA-256 of each file before the patch (or accepts the recorded result), applies it, verifies the result, and records it in the configure fingerprint. Add an entry only with a reason and a removal condition (docs/porting/crtweb_porting.md).

patches.reason: WTF::RawHex gives int64_t/uint64_t their own constructors only for CPU(ADDRESS32) or OS(DARWIN); elsewhere it assumes int64_t is intptr_t (true for Linux/Bionic LP64). CRT presents macOS to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (no __APPLE__), but the compiler's integer types stay Darwin's (int64_t is long long, intptr_t is long): clang's own arm_acle.h/arm_neon.h and builtins require uint64_t == __UINT64_TYPE__, so the typedef cannot be changed (tried: clang crashed). RawHex(uint64_t) was therefore ambiguous in JavaScriptCore/tools/Integrity.cpp. The patch adds one more condition, selected by -DWTF_CRT_INT64_IS_LONG_LONG which the harness passes on macOS.
patches.remove_when: WebKit selects the int64_t overloads by type identity (std::is_same_v<int64_t, intptr_t>) instead of OS(DARWIN), or CRT presents macOS to WTF as OS(DARWIN) without pulling in Apple SDK code.

patches.reason: JavaScriptCore's inline assembler for the offlineasm LLInt and its thunks takes the assembler syntax from OS(DARWIN): the `_` symbol prefix (SYMBOL_STRING), `.private_extern _x` versus `.hidden x` (HIDE_SYMBOL), the local label prefix `L` versus `.L`, `.alt_entry`, and the absence of `.cfi_startproc` in the global asm blocks. Those are properties of the Mach-O object format, not of the OS, but CRT presents macOS to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (no __APPLE__; see 0001), so the ELF spellings were chosen and would not link or assemble. The patch ORs one more condition, selected by -DWTF_CRT_MACHO_ASM which the harness passes on macOS in baseline-jit mode, into those conditionals (the three in WTF/InlineASM.h, the alt-entry and two cfi conditionals in llint/LowLevelInterpreter.cpp, the `#if OS(DARWIN)` guard offlineasm itself writes into LLIntAssembly.h, and the two `#if OS(DARWIN)` guards arm64.rb writes for Mach-O versus ELF relocation specifiers (`@PAGE`/`@GOTPAGE` versus `:lo12:`/`:got:`)). offlineasm also emits ELF `.size`/`.type` debug directives whenever CMake passes --binary-format=ELF, which it does for CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME Linux, so asm.rb additionally skips them when the environment variable WTF_CRT_MACHO_ASM is set (the harness sets it).
patches.remove_when: WebKit keys the assembler syntax on the object format (__MACH__/__ELF__/_WIN32) instead of OS(DARWIN), or CRT presents macOS as OS(DARWIN) without Apple SDK code.

files.license_basis: directory-level license file Source/JavaScriptCore/COPYING.LIB (GNU Library GPL, LGPL-2); the file has no header of its own

patches.reason: CRT presents Windows to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (libcrtweb/cmake/crt_webkit_platform.cmake), so JavaScriptCore's offlineasm and inline assembly take their ELF branches, but the object format is COFF and the assembler rejects the ELF-only forms (found by the Windows baseline-jit build: `.hidden`, `.size` and `.type name, function` are `unknown directive`/`expected absolute expression`, `.previous` is an unknown directive, and a `name@plt` reference does not exist in COFF). Selected by -DWTF_CRT_COFF_ASM (compiler side) and the WTF_CRT_COFF_ASM environment variable (offlineasm side), both set by tools/build_webkit_jsc.py on Windows: HIDE_SYMBOL expands to nothing, GLOBAL_REFERENCE is the plain symbol, the ELF debug directives are not emitted, and the `.previous` after the probe trampolines and the unary-double thunks (an ELF section-stack directive; nothing follows them in the same asm block) is dropped. Mach-O has its own variant (0002).
patches.remove_when: WebKit selects these directives by object format (COFF/ELF/Mach-O) instead of OS(), or CRT presents Windows to WTF as OS(WINDOWS) without pulling in windows.h and the Microsoft C runtime.

patches.reason: CRT presents macOS to WebKit as OS(LINUX) to select the Bionic/Linux-shaped source surface, but generated code still follows the actual Darwin arm64 object and calling-convention ABI. ARM64Registers.h's Linux branch marks x18 allocatable, while Darwin reserves x18 as the platform register. Under FTL/B3 register pressure that mismatch let generated code use x18 across a runtime call and produced a null-address write near operationStringFromCharCode. The harness defines WTF_CRT_DARWIN_ARM64_ABI only for macOS arm64, selecting WebKit's existing non-Linux register table without enabling Apple SDK source branches; Linux/aarch64 is unchanged.
patches.remove_when: WebKit derives the x18 reservation from the target ABI/object format rather than OS(LINUX), or CRT can select WebKit's Darwin ABI traits independently of its Apple SDK source surface.

files.license_basis: no header of its own; the build files around it in Source/cmake carry the Apple BSD-2-Clause notice (47 of the directory's 96 files; none carry another license), and the file belongs to the same Apple-authored CMake build system

patches.reason: WebKitCommon.cmake accepts only the ports in ALL_PORTS and stops with 'Please choose which WebKit port to build' for any other -DPORT. The CRT port is a new port (Source/cmake/OptionsCRT.cmake and the per-module PlatformCRT.cmake files are new CRT-owned files, libcrtweb/port); its name has to be in that list. Everything else the port needs is selected by file name (Options${PORT}.cmake, Platform${PORT}.cmake) or by -DWTF_PLATFORM_CRT=1, as the PlayStation port does, so this is the only change to an existing file for milestone B1.
patches.remove_when: Never as long as CRT carries its own port: a port that is not upstream has to be registered. It is a one-line, rebase-friendly change.

files.license_basis: no header of its own; the build files of the tree (Source/cmake) carry the Apple BSD-2-Clause notice and the file belongs to the same Apple-authored CMake build system

patches.reason: On a Darwin build host the top-level CMakeLists.txt includes WebKitXcodeSDK.cmake before project(), which resolves an Apple SDK with xcrun, pins Xcode's compilers and tools, and stops with 'Building for an Apple platform without an SDK directory (CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT) or supported PORT variable' for any port other than Mac, IOS and JSCOnly. The CRT port is not an Apple port: it builds against the CRT sysroot with the CRT toolchain file and compilers, and presents macOS to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (patches 0001, 0002, 0004; Host ABI firewall), so it must not select an Apple SDK at all. The patch skips the include for PORT=CRT.
patches.remove_when: WebKit decides on the SDK from the target (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME/CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE) instead of the build host, or accepts a port that opts out of Apple SDK resolution.

patches.reason: Nine WebCore files select per-port types and behaviour with PLATFORM(PLAYSTATION) (the accessibility wrapper class, the RenderTheme/PlatformRenderTheme base, ChromeClient accessibility notifications, the SQLite extras, ICU searcher variants). PlatformCRT compiles the PlayStation port's own files for these roles (docs/acceptance/crtweb_acceptance.md, 3B plan), so it must take the same branches; defining WTF_PLATFORM_PLAYSTATION as well was rejected because 28 sites in WTF and the PlatformEnable/PlatformHave headers would then change for every module and JavaScriptCore and WebCore would no longer see the same macros. Each hunk only widens PLATFORM(PLAYSTATION) to (PLATFORM(PLAYSTATION) || PLATFORM(CRT)).
patches.remove_when: Upstream adds a CRT (or a generic non-GLib) platform guard, or the files are replaced by CRT-owned implementations of the same roles; rebase by re-running the same textual widening.

patches.reason: Page::filterRenderingModes() calls Settings::hardwareAccelerationEnabled() for every Skia platform except Windows and WPE-without-WPEPlatform, but the HardwareAccelerationEnabled preference exists only for PLATFORM(GTK) || ENABLE(WPE_PLATFORM) (Source/WTF/Scripts/Preferences/UnifiedWebPreferences.yaml). A Skia port that is neither (Skia is upstream's only 2D renderer at this commit, but only GTK/WPE build with it) fails to compile. The CRT port paints on the CPU and has no hardware-acceleration setting, so it takes the software branch.
patches.remove_when: Upstream makes the call conditional on the preference's own condition, or the preference's condition includes the other Skia ports.

patches.reason: WTF::Persistence::Encoder/Decoder give the fixed-width integers their own overloads and send every other arithmetic type to the Coder<T> template, which has no coder for it. The WebKit tree assumes size_t is uint64_t (true for Linux/Bionic LP64); under the CRT macOS persona the integer typedefs stay Darwin's (uint64_t is unsigned long long, size_t is unsigned long; see 0001), so WebCore's generic KeyedEncoder/KeyedDecoder (the PlayStation/CRT keyed coders: size_t counts) stopped at 'implicit instantiation of undefined template Coder<unsigned long>'. The patch adds unsigned long and long overloads that forward to the fixed-width ones, selected by -DWTF_CRT_INT64_IS_LONG_LONG which the harness already passes on macOS.
patches.remove_when: WTF selects the persistence overloads by type identity (std::is_same_v<size_t, uint64_t>) or has coders for size_t on every platform, or CRT presents macOS as OS(DARWIN) without Apple SDK code.

patches.reason: Source/WebKit selects the PlayStation port's per-port members, event classes and behaviour with PLATFORM(PLAYSTATION): the Web/Network process paths in ProcessLaunchOptions and WebProcessPool, the libwpe-based NativeWeb*Event classes, the select()-based socket monitor of IPC::Connection (the generic RunLoop has no file-descriptor sources), WebsiteDataStore directories, ChromeClient accessibility notifications. PlatformCRT compiles the PlayStation port's files for the same roles (docs/acceptance/crtweb_acceptance.md, 3B plan), so it must take the same branches. Each hunk only widens PLATFORM(PLAYSTATION) to (PLATFORM(PLAYSTATION) || PLATFORM(CRT)); WTF_PLATFORM_PLAYSTATION itself is not defined (see patch 0007). DrawingAreaCoordinatedGraphics.cpp is deliberately not widened: its PlayStation-only include of LayerTreeHostPlayStation.h belongs to a compositor path upstream no longer builds.
patches.remove_when: Upstream adds a CRT (or a generic non-GLib) platform guard, or the guarded code moves to per-port files; rebase by re-running the same textual widening.

patches.reason: WKBase.h and WKAPICast.h include the platform-specific base and cast headers by compiler macros (BUILDING_GTK__, BUILDING_WPE__, __APPLE__, _WIN32, __SCE__). The CRT port exposes the PlayStation-shaped C API (WKView, WKRunLoop), whose WKViewRef and its casts are declared in WKBasePlayStation.h and WKAPICastPlayStation.h, so it takes those branches.
patches.remove_when: Upstream adds a per-port selection hook, or CRT's C API stops being PlayStation-shaped (the crtweb API of Tranche 4 hides WebKit's headers).

patches.reason: WEBKIT_COPY_FILES copies framework headers into <build>/<framework>/Headers except on Apple platforms, where it symlinks so that #import deduplicates a header reachable both as <WebKit/X.h> and through the source tree. Clang's #pragma once does the same only for the same file: with copies, a translation unit that gets WKPageUIClient.h from the precompiled prefix header by its source path and again as <WebKit/WKPageUIClient.h> from the build tree redefines every enumerator (26 files at B4). GCC deduplicates by content and time stamp, which is why the Linux ports do not meet it. PlatformCRT builds with clang, so it takes the symlink branch; OptionsCRT sets CRT_SYMLINK_FRAMEWORK_HEADERS only on hosts that can create symlinks.
patches.remove_when: Upstream symlinks (or hard-links) framework headers on every platform, or the prefix headers include the framework-style path.

patches.reason: DrawingArea::create picks the drawing area by platform macro: Cocoa, WC, or one of two Coordinated Graphics flavours (the GLib/GL one for GTK and WPE, a PlayStation-era one for the rest). The second no longer builds against LayerTreeHost, and the first needs GLib, EGL and a GPU. PlatformCRT supplies its own (DrawingAreaCRT, libcrtweb/port) and this patch is the hook that selects it.
patches.remove_when: Upstream adds a platform drawing-area registration point, or PlatformCRT paints through a maintained shared drawing area.

license_policy.rule: A file this manifest modifies keeps its upstream license and header; the patch is a derivative under that license, so every entry records the class of the modified file (from tools/scan_webkit_headers.py) and it must be one CRT can carry: LGPL-2/2.1 (WebKit's own LGPL code), BSD-2/3-Clause (Apple's and most WebKit code) or another permissive class. A file CRT adds is a *new CRT-owned file*, listed under new_files with the project default license (LICENSE.md, BSD-2-Clause) and its header. Never mix: no CRT code is added to an LGPL file beyond the patch itself.
allowed_for_modified_files: no-license-header (only with a license_basis naming the directory-level license file)
